title: The estimate is total effort, in one stored field. Remaining effort is derived as the total minus logged minutes
Remaining effort is not clamped: it reaches zero and goes negative, and the negative is shown, because running long is information
Two doors into that one field: the total can be set directly, and the remaining can be set, which writes the logged time plus the new remaining as the total
A ready task keeps a positive estimate: clearing the estimate of a ready task is refused, with an error saying the task must move to the inbox first or keep a positive estimate
Ready meaning a positive estimate is an invariant throughout the specification, and an edit to one field must not change a task's status behind the caller's back
A task never claims negative effort: an unfinished task at or below zero receives a five-minute completion slot as a planning placeholder, but only while it is not running
While a timer runs, the running block is the claim, so an overrun keeps growing and pushes the rest of the day's plan later until it is stopped; stopping or completing it brings the slot back
Any task at or below zero remaining effort raises a persistent estimate_overrun notice at level info, whose point is to ask the human to revise the total
The application never rewrites the estimate towards logged time, and completion is never automatic
Editing or deleting a time entry recalculates remaining effort and can clear the overrun
Pausing stops the timer and keeps the task in progress; pausing is a task act, not the end of the day
Starting another task returns the previous one to ready unless it was completed or cancelled
Concurrent work, behind a configuration flag: with the flag off, exactly the single-timer treatment above holds; the flag defaults to off
With it on, a second task may start while another runs, without stopping it, but only when the caller asks for that explicitly; an ordinary start while something runs fails
The pause heuristic survives the flag, so a paused task returns to ready when something else starts after it
§3.5's "at most one task MAY be in progress" and §3.12's "at most one entry MAY be open" become conditional when concurrency is on
The tray and the active indicator show a list rather than one task when concurrency is on
A manual entry must not overlap any open entry
Ending the day stops every open timer at its stop time
Starting work on a task before the day has been started is refused, not inferred: the API and the agent interface fail with an error saying a session must be started first
The client offers to start the session in place as part of that interaction
The estimate is retained on completion and cancellation and displayed with the logged minutes, so the guess and the outcome stay side by side
session-and-timetable: ending the day stops every open timer at its stop time, and start-day is the precondition for starting work
architecture: ForTrackingTime carries the concurrency setting and the day-started precondition, and the active task is a set rather than a single value
decisions-forecast-warnings: estimate_overrun is persistent, and no forecast may treat a task that is running and over its estimate as out of work
decisions-agent-interface: a concurrent start carries explicit intent, and a start without a session fails with a named error
child-efforts: the tray and the active indicator show a list when concurrency is on, and the estimate surface offers both doors
